Case 31 – Employees Federal Credit Union

Summary of Data Analysis: R3, R6 and R4a–c

Author

Cecilia Espina

Published

November 16, 2026

Overview

What this report does. It answers five research questions about Employees Federal Credit Union (EFCU) members using the cleaned survey file (128 members; 57 live in the headquarters area, 71 elsewhere). Each section starts with the descriptive story; test statistics appear only in parentheses.

# Research question Variables Analysis
R3 How do members rate the proficiency of credit union employees? Q3–Q6 (employee index) Descriptives; one-sample t-test vs. neutral (3)
R6 How effectively do members think the credit union is operated? Q30–Q34, Q37r Descriptives; one-sample t-tests vs. neutral (3)
R4a Do members in the headquarters area and elsewhere differ in their views on borrowing? Q8r, Q30, Q27 Welch t-tests; chi-square test of independence
R4b …in their views on the services provided? Q7r, Q31–Q34 Welch t-tests
R4c …in their overall view of management and of employees? Q37r, employee index Welch t-tests

R3 · Employee proficiency

R3 · Descriptive statistics

Members think very highly of the credit union’s employees. About nine in ten agree that employees are courteous (90%) and helpful (88%), and about four in five say they are professional (82%) and always available (79%). Availability is also the only item where any real disagreement shows up (3%).

The four items hang together well (Cronbach’s α = 0.87), so I averaged them into one employee proficiency index. It averages 4.21 out of 5 (SD = 0.59), and 76% of members have an index of 4 or higher (Table 1 and Figure 1).

Insight: employees are EFCU’s clearest strength. Nobody rates the index below neutral, and the only soft spot is availability.

R3 · One-sample t-test

Is this more than a polite “neutral”? Yes. Every item and the index sit well above the neutral midpoint of 3 (index: t(127) = 22.95, p < .001; Table 2), and the index is even above “agree” (4) (t(127) = 3.91, p < .001). The distance from neutral is large for every item, and smallest for availability (M = 4.08).

R6 · Effectiveness of operations

R6 · Descriptive statistics

Members also see the credit union as well run, but less enthusiastically than they see its employees. Overall, 84% rate management and operation as good or excellent (M = 4.07; 121 members gave an opinion). Confidentiality is the highest-rated specific item (78% agree). Roughly six in ten agree that loan applications are processed promptly (60%), that the services meet members’ needs (59%) and that applications are simple (58%), with about a third unsure. The weak spot is pricing: only 30% agree that EFCU’s loan rates are lower than other institutions’, 46% are unsure and 24% disagree (Table 3 and Figure 2).

The four operations statements (Q31–Q34) are only weakly related (α = 0.47), so I did not combine them into a composite and analyze each item on its own.

Insight: EFCU is seen as well run, but “good” rather than “great”. Members trust it with their information; they are far less sure it is cheaper than the competition.

R6 · One-sample t-tests

Compared with the neutral midpoint (3), members are positive about the overall management and operation (t(120) = 16.13, p < .001), confidentiality (t(127) = 15.74, p < .001), prompt processing (t(127) = 10.25, p < .001), meeting needs (t(127) = 9.87, p < .001) and application simplicity (t(127) = 6.66, p < .001) (Table 4). The one item that does not differ from neutral is the belief that loan rates are lower than elsewhere (t(127) = 0.82, p = .416): on average members are undecided.

R4a · Borrowing: headquarters area vs. elsewhere

R4a · Descriptive statistics

The clearest difference between the two groups is actual borrowing. 35% of members in the headquarters area currently have an EFCU loan, compared with 54% of members elsewhere (Table 5 and Figure 3). Opinions about loan rates are similar: both groups see rates as about average, although headquarters-area members lean slightly lower (Q8r M = 2.98 vs. 3.26) while members elsewhere lean slightly “high”. Both groups are unsure whether EFCU’s rates beat competitors’ (Q30 M = 3.14 vs. 3.00) (Table 6).

R4a · Chi-square test of independence

Members who live near headquarters are less likely to hold an EFCU loan (χ²(1) = 4.34, p = .037). The result is borderline: with a continuity correction p = .057, and Fisher’s exact test gives p = .049.

R4a · Independent-samples t-tests

Opinions about rates do not differ clearly. Headquarters-area members see loan rates as somewhat lower than other members do, a small-to-medium gap that just misses significance (t(97.4) = -1.95, p = .055; d = -0.38), and agreement that EFCU’s rates beat competitors’ is the same in both groups (t(124.6) = 0.92, p = .359) (Table 6). Q8r has 107 answers, because members with no opinion are missing.

Insight: headquarters-area members borrow less even though they do not see EFCU’s rates as worse (if anything, as slightly lower). Price does not seem to explain the gap, so the next section looks at the application process.

R4b · Services: headquarters area vs. elsewhere

R4b · Descriptive statistics

Views of the services are almost identical in the two groups. Confidentiality, prompt processing, meeting needs and savings rates all differ by less than a fifth of a scale point (Figure 4). The exception is the ease of loan applications: headquarters-area members rate them lower (Q34 M = 3.28 vs. 3.61).

R4b · Independent-samples t-tests

Welch tests agree: only application simplicity differs, with headquarters-area members less likely to find applications simple (t(94.2) = -2.28, p = .025; d = -0.42). Savings rates (t(101.9) = -0.47, p = .639), confidentiality (t(121.3) = 1.62, p = .109), prompt processing (t(118.9) = -0.44, p = .661) and meeting needs (t(112.9) = 0.04, p = .968) show no difference (Table 7). With five comparisons, a single p near .05 should be read cautiously.

Insight: headquarters-area members borrow less and find the loan application harder. That is a lead worth testing (a simpler application process aimed at them), not proof that the application is the reason.

R4c · Overall management and employees: headquarters area vs. elsewhere

R4c · Independent-samples t-tests

Overall impressions are the same in both groups. The overall rating of management and operation is 4.02 in the headquarters area vs. 4.10 elsewhere (t(118.7) = -0.66, p = .513), and the employee proficiency index is 4.28 vs. 4.14 (t(122.5) = 1.30, p = .195) (Table 8). Q37r has 121 answers, because members with no opinion are missing.

Insight: location does not change members’ overall verdict. Wherever they live, members think EFCU is well managed and its employees are excellent.

Key takeaways

  1. R3 – Employees: a clear strength (index 4.21 of 5); availability is the only slightly weaker item.
  2. R6 – Operations: seen as well run (84% good or excellent) and trustworthy with information, but members are undecided on whether rates beat the competition.
  3. R4a – Borrowing: 35% of headquarters-area members hold an EFCU loan vs. 54% elsewhere, with no worse opinion of rates.
  4. R4b – Services: the two groups agree on everything except the ease of the loan application, which headquarters-area members rate lower.
  5. R4c – Overall: no difference in overall management or employee ratings.

Recommendation: investigate why headquarters-area members borrow less (for example, with a short follow-up on the application experience) and use members’ confidence in confidentiality and staff to promote EFCU loans.

Notes on method

  • Data: cleaned SPSS file (N = 128). Q7r, Q8r and Q37r follow the Module 10 recoding, where “no opinion” answers are missing and excluded from those analyses.
  • Employee proficiency index = mean of Q3–Q6, computed directly from the four items.
  • Likert items are treated as interval scales, as in the Data Analysis Table. One-sample tests compare each item with the neutral midpoint (3); group comparisons use Welch’s t-test (unequal variances). Cohen’s d is the effect size.
  • Cronbach’s α was used only to decide whether to form a composite (Q3–Q6: yes; Q31–Q34: no). The factor analysis reported in the earlier activity is not repeated here.
  • No correction for multiple comparisons was applied, so isolated p values near .05 should be read cautiously.
